propositions: A one-time backfill script measures cyclomatic complexity and clone counts at sampled historical commits by running lizard and jscpd tools and writing snapshots through the standard snapshot writer.

The timestamp of each backfilled snapshot must be the sampled commit's committer date (via git show -s --format=%cI), not the wall-clock time of the backfill run, to preserve historical trend integrity.
When a metric tool is absent or fails for a sampled commit, measure_tree returns None and that commit is skipped with logging but does not abort the backfill.
Each written snapshot is tagged with source='snapshot' and confidence='high' to indicate deterministic tool-based provenance.

The test suite stubs measure_tree to return mock complexity and clone_count integers, verifying 3 snapshots are written with correct ts values and integer-typed metrics without requiring external tools.
